posts.note: Review of two published negative trials; the analysis is retrospective. 'We have every reason to believe this trial will yield something' narrates a pre-result expectation about an already published trial, so it was not logged. Only the Radial sponsor blurb ('soon, eCOT-AS by Neurolief') is forward-looking.
Central claim is a generic prognosis (most kids will be ok), logged as borderline. Present-tense trend line on youth attempts logged with forward_looking false. Radial sponsor blurb logged.
Part one of a Wizard of Oz health-insurance parody. Lines of fictional characters were not logged. Author-voice teasers about the newsletter and a dated regulatory line in footnote 9 were logged.

Parody part two. Dr. Skinman's lines are fictional and were not logged. Logged: the intro promise of more Radial content, a footnote teaser about PBMs, and a generic autoimmune prognosis in footnote 1. Footnote 12 ('Currently, insurance will not authorize...') is a present-tense payer description, not logged.
Parody part three. Radial sponsor blurb and a hyperbolic insurer-consolidation line in footnote 3 were logged.
Parody part four. The Founder's lines are fictional. Footnote 1 holds thought experiments (readers' insurance) and general truisms, not logged. Only the Radial sponsor blurb was logged.

statements.quote: However, it is perfectly reasonable to say, to parents and kids, in the fallout after a suicide attempt, that the most likely outcome, by a mile, is that the kids will be ok.
statements.context: The author reads Bommersbach et al., JAMA Psychiatry 2025: 164 early adolescents (age 10 to 14) followed up to 36 years after a first suicide attempt; none died by suicide and 80 percent had good long-term outcomes. He generalizes this to what parents should expect after an attempt.
statements.note: Generic clinical prognosis, not a dated world event. Restated in the post as 'most kids will live' and 'On average, it’s going to be ok.' Borderline.

statements.quote: No, it’s not about fewer suicide attempts among youth. That keeps going up.
statements.context: Opening of the post. The author says the good news is not a fall in youth suicide attempts, which he says keep rising, especially among girls.
statements.note: Present-tense trend statement; continuation of the rise is only implicit. Logged as borderline.
